spec.title: Running versions
spec.description: A version live at any point in a bucket fills it, so two rows overlap across an upgrade.

spec.title: Requests by handler
spec.description: The busiest handlers, by route template: `/d/:uid/:slug` is one series whatever dashboard was opened. Ranking is per point, so a wide range can surface more than five handlers.

spec.expr:
sum by (handler) (rate(grafana_http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="prometheus.scrape.grafana"}[$__rate_interval]))
and
topk(5, sum by (handler) (rate(grafana_http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="prometheus.scrape.grafana"}[$__range])))

spec.title: Requests in flight
spec.description:
Peak concurrency per bucket.
- A constant floor is a long-lived request such as the live websocket.
- A rising floor means requests arrive faster than they finish.

spec.title: p99 by handler
spec.description:
Ordered by traffic; a handler with a handful of requests can top the p99 on one slow call.
- Rows at roughly 5 ms sit in the histogram's first bucket; their order means nothing.

spec.title: Errors
spec.description:
HTTP responses Grafana answered with an error. The HTTP tab attributes both classes to a handler.
- `5xx` is the class to act on, on the right axis.
- `4xx` leaves out `/api/live/ws`: a tab with an expired session retries the websocket and draws a `401` every few seconds.

spec.title: Uptime
spec.description: **Running versions** says whether the last restart was a deploy.

spec.title: Requests by plugin and endpoint
spec.description:
Backend calls Grafana makes into datasource plugins; the built-in `-- Grafana --` datasource is excluded.
- `queryData` — panel and alert queries.
- `callResource` — the label and metadata lookups editors make.
- Datasources of the same type share one plugin process and one series.

spec.title: Errors and cancellations
spec.description:
An unreachable datasource shows up here; the latency panels measure only the calls that got an answer.
- `downstream` blames the datasource the plugin called.
- `plugin` blames the plugin itself.
- `cancelled` is the browser or the alert evaluation walking away before the plugin answered, across all plugins.

spec.title: Latency p99
spec.description:
Time from Grafana's call into the plugin until the response: the datasource round trip and frame decoding.
- A series is a plugin type, not one datasource: every Loki datasource is inside `loki`.
- A gap of more than an order of magnitude over p50 means a small share of queries is doing all the waiting.

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, plugin_id, endpoint) (rate(grafana_plugin_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="prometheus.scrape.grafana", plugin_id!="grafana"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

spec.title: Latency p50
spec.description: What a panel load actually waits on; `Latency p99` above is the tail, on the same log axis.

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le, plugin_id, endpoint) (rate(grafana_plugin_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="prometheus.scrape.grafana", plugin_id!="grafana"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

spec.title: Alert instances by state
spec.description:
One instance per series a rule returns: a rule over a series per host produces one per host, so instances outnumber rules.
- `normal` is drawn only after a click in the legend; its count stays there.

spec.title: Evaluation failures
spec.description:
Rule evaluations that hit an error.
- `failed attempts` counts every try; the scheduler retries, so most of these still produce a result.
- `failed evaluations` ran out of retries: the rule kept its previous state for that interval.

spec.title: Scheduler behind
spec.description: How far the evaluation scheduler is running behind its own tick. Sustained growth means rules cannot be evaluated as fast as their interval demands.

spec.title: API latency
spec.description:
Requests to the alerting endpoints, the rule editor and the ruler API included.
- The bottom band is the first bucket, 5 ms; nothing inside it can be separated.
- Traffic comes from someone having the UI open, so an empty column is an idle period rather than an outage.

spec.title: Datasource queries / sec
spec.description: Queries Grafana sent into datasource plugins on behalf of panels and alert rules. The number is the latest rate.

spec.title: Notifications
spec.description:
Notifications per contact-point integration, delivered or not.
- A quiet stretch means no alert changed state.

spec.title: Rules by state
spec.description: Rules the scheduler has loaded. A step change without a deploy means someone edited rules in the UI. A paused rule stays loaded and stops evaluating.

spec.title: CPU
spec.description: CPU time as a share of one core: 250% is 2.5 cores. Dashboards render in the browser, so this is query proxying, alert evaluation and the database.

spec.title: Memory
spec.description: Resident memory sits above the Go heap: it also covers stacks, mmap'ed regions and allocator overhead. Read `next GC target` against `Go heap in use` — the runtime collects harder as the heap approaches it.

spec.title: Goroutines
spec.description: Sustained growth against a flat request rate is a leak.

spec.title: Database connections
spec.description:
Grafana's database pools, `grafana` and `unified_storage` summed; the stack is the open connections.
- `max open` is drawn only when a limit is configured. Without one the pool grows on demand and no request waits for a connection.

spec.title: Live users
spec.description: Open Grafana Live websockets — people with a Grafana tab in front of them right now.

spec.title: Database connections closed
spec.description: Why the pool discards connections. Steady `max_idle_time` churn is normal; `max_lifetime` churn under load costs a reconnect each time.

spec.title: Annotations
spec.description: Annotation rows in the Grafana database. Alert state changes write one each, so the count only falls when the annotation cleanup trims it.

spec.title: Dashboards
spec.description: A step down is a bulk deletion — provisioning removing more than intended shows up here first.

spec.title: Service account tokens
spec.description: Tokens outnumbering accounts is normal — rotation leaves both live until the old one is revoked.

spec.title: Alert rules
spec.description: Rules the scheduler has loaded, across all groups.

spec.title: Users
spec.description:
Accounts, and those active in the last 30 days, so every line but `live` moves in steps.
- `live` is open Grafana Live websockets — people with a Grafana tab in front of them.
- The role lines split the active users; a user with roles in several orgs counts in each, so they can sum past `active (30d)`.

spec.title: Firing alerts
spec.description: Alert instances currently in `alerting`. Pending and normal instances are broken out on the Alerting tab.

spec.title: Status
spec.description: Share of requests that failed on each path: 5xx for HTTP, plugin errors for datasources, evaluations the scheduler could not complete for alerting. Client errors are counted on the HTTP and Datasources tabs.

spec.title: Requests / sec
spec.description: All HTTP Grafana served, its own polling included. The number is the latest rate.

spec.title: Errors by handler
spec.description:
`4xx` and `5xx` together; `Overview / Errors` splits them by class.
- `4xx` from `/api/live/ws` is left out: an expired session's tab retries the websocket with a `401` every few seconds.

spec.expr:
sum by (handler) (
  increase(grafana_http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="prometheus.scrape.grafana", status_code=~"5.."}[$__interval])
  or
  increase(grafana_http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="prometheus.scrape.grafana", status_code=~"4..", handler!="/api/live/ws"}[$__interval])
) > 0

spec.title: Datasource latency
spec.description: Every datasource pooled, so this is what a panel load waits on whichever one served it. The Datasources tab splits it per plugin and endpoint.

spec.title: Datasource requests
spec.description: Outcome of the queries datasource plugins returned to Grafana. The Datasources tab splits the same traffic per plugin.

spec.title: HTTP error ratio
spec.description: Share of requests answered 5xx; `Overview · Errors` counts client errors too.

spec.expr:
{syslog_id="docker/grafana"}
|= `$contains`
| detected_level =~ `$errors_only`
| drop hostname, job, project, service_name, syslog_id, systemd_unit, transport

topk(15, sum by (detected_level, msg) (count_over_time({syslog_id="docker/grafana"}
  | logfmt msg
  | msg != ``
[$__range])))

spec.title: Failed attempts by reason
spec.description: The error class behind `failed attempts` on `Evaluation failures`, and how many distinct rules hit each one. Parsed from the alert scheduler log.

spec.expr:
sum by (reason) (count_over_time({syslog_id="docker/grafana"}
  |= `Failed to evaluate rule`
  | regexp `\[(?P<reason>[a-zA-Z0-9._]+)\]`
[$__range]))

count by (reason) (sum by (reason, rule_uid) (count_over_time({syslog_id="docker/grafana"}
  |= `Failed to evaluate rule`
  | logfmt rule_uid
  | regexp `\[(?P<reason>[a-zA-Z0-9._]+)\]`
[$__range])))

spec.title: Datasources
spec.description: Configured datasources, all types; on the Datasources tab, one plugin series carries all of a type.

spec.title: HTTP requests
spec.description: Grafana's own polling — alert state, live — dominates the 2xx line and holds the baseline above zero.

spec.title: HTTP latency
spec.description: All handlers pooled, Grafana's own polling included, so the median tracks its cheapest internal calls. `HTTP / p99 by handler` attributes the tail.

spec.name: errors_only
spec.label: Errors only
spec.description: Show only warnings and errors in the log. Lines Loki cannot classify are kept — their level is unknown, not low.

spec.name: contains
spec.label: Contains
spec.description: Substring the log line must contain, on top of the Errors only switch. Matches are highlighted.
